title: Shopping Cart — bug, feature, optimize
description: A tiny shopping cart library is failing tests. Diagnose and fix, then add discount-code support, then optimize the price loop.

checkpoints.label: Bug fix
checkpoints.prompt: Three tests in `tests/test_checkpoint.py` fail. Find the bug in `cart.py` and fix it. Don't change the tests.

checkpoints.label: Feature: discount codes
checkpoints.prompt: Implement `apply_discount_code(cart, code)` in `cart.py`. Codes are loaded from `discounts.json`. Make the tests in `tests/test_checkpoint.py` pass.

checkpoints.label: Optimize
checkpoints.prompt: `total(cart)` is O(n*m) over items × discounts. Make it O(n+m) without changing the API. Tests cover correctness; the timing harness `tests/test_checkpoint.py::test_perf` enforces the bound.

items.label: Correctness
items.prompt: Did all checkpoint tests pass at submit time?

items.label: Code quality
items.prompt: Is the final code idiomatic Python? Naming, structure, type hints, no dead code.

items.label: Design
items.prompt: Are the bug fix, feature, and optimization integrated cleanly? No layering violations or duplicated logic.

items.label: Verification habits
items.prompt: Examining the chat history, did the candidate verify AI suggestions or accept them blindly? This is a coaching signal, not a punishment — explain what you see.
